sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我对待健康的方式有了很大的改变。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 过去我总是专注于追求极致，想要做得更多。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 但现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my Whoop.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我如此沉迷于我的Whoop。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person.
sentences.zh: 说真的，你们知道我是一个非常依赖数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain, is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开Whoop应用程序，看看我的睡眠、压力和身体负荷如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及日常感受相关联。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么精英运动员，但我确实从中受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很喜欢深入了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day-to-day
sentences.zh: Whoop还为我提供了可操作的个性化见解，这让我变得更有主见，也意味着我在日常生活中能做出更明智的决定，

sentences.en: about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 清楚自己需要什么，而不是一味地踩油门，不停地向前冲。

sentences.zh: 新用户在订阅会员之前，可以先通过Whoop的30天免费试用进行体验。

sentences.zh: 有些物品我们一直珍藏，是因为它们能瞬间把我们带回某个时刻。

sentences.en: A photo, a piece of clothing, a tiny souvenir from somewhere unforgettable.
sentences.zh: 一张照片、一件衣服、或是某个难忘之地带回的小纪念品。

sentences.en: In my new podcast, Charmed, with Sam Todd, we explore the memories, obsessions, and personal treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 在我的新播客《Charmed, with Sam Todd》中，我们将探索那些成为我们生命一部分的记忆、执念和个人珍宝。

sentences.en: From the sublime all the way to the absolutely ridiculous, it's a fascinating deep dive into the keepsakes we hold close and the memories that make them special.
sentences.zh: 从崇高到极其荒诞，这是一次深入挖掘我们珍视的纪念品以及赋予它们特殊意义的记忆的迷人旅程。

sentences.en: Charmed, with me, Sam Todd.

sentences.en: And you can actually catch the model thinking, I think X is actually true, but I'm going to tell the user why.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以捕捉到模型在思考，比如“我觉得X其实是真的，但我打算告诉用户为什么”。

sentences.zh: 我是Walter Isaacson。

sentences.zh: 在我的新播客《The Builders》中，

sentences.en: I'm going inside the minds of the people shaping our future.
sentences.zh: 我将深入探究那些塑造我们未来的人们的思想。

sentences.en: Listen to The Builders starting October 13th on the iHeart Radio app, Apple Podcasts, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 从10月13日开始，请在iHeart Radio应用程序、Apple Podcasts或任何你获取播客的地方收听《The Builders》。

sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，这是一档探讨我们在20多岁时经历的一些重大人生变化和转折的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcast for another episode, another bonus episode, I should say.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客收听新的一期，应该说是另一期加更节目。

sentences.en: Welcome.
sentences.zh: 欢迎。

sentences.en: If you are listening to this right now, you are one of my top listeners.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在正在听这一期，那你就是我最忠实的听众之一。

sentences.en: You're one of my paid subscribers.
sentences.zh: 你是我的付费订阅者之一。

sentences.en: I just want to say a huge thank you.
sentences.zh: 我只想说一声非常感谢。

sentences.en: I've got you all in one place, all right here.
sentences.zh: 把你们都聚在一起，就在这里。

sentences.en: So I just want to say thank you so much for, you know, wanting to listen to the sound of my voice multiple times a week.
sentences.zh: 所以我只想说非常感谢你们，你知道，愿意每周多次听到我的声音。

sentences.en: It is, I don't know, a weird feeling, but I'm so, so grateful that you care about this podcast, you care about this show, and you care about what we're trying to do,
sentences.zh: 这是一种，我不知道，一种奇怪的感觉，但我真的非常、非常感激你们关心这个播客，关心这个节目，关心我们正在尝试做的事情，

sentences.en: which is apply psychology, something that can often seem really inaccessible and distant to every area of our life, every area of our life in our 20s,
sentences.zh: 那就是将心理学——一种通常看起来非常深奥和遥远的东西——应用到我们生活的方方面面，我们20多岁生活的方方面面，

sentences.en: and hopefully learn something new every week about what we're experiencing, what we go through, and how that interacts with our mental well-being
sentences.zh: 并希望每周都能学到一些关于我们正在经历的事情、我们所遭遇的一切，以及它们如何与我们的心理健康相互作用的新知识，

sentences.en: and the psychological processes that underpin it.
sentences.zh: 以及支撑这一切的心理过程。

sentences.en: So I just want to say a huge thank you to all of you who are listening to this episode right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我只想对现在正在收听这一期的你们所有人说一声非常感谢。

sentences.en: You guys chose the topic this week as well.
sentences.zh: 这一周的话题也是你们选出来的。

sentences.en: We're talking about microhabits.
sentences.zh: 我们今天要聊的是“微习惯”。

sentences.en: I gave you guys two options on my Instagram, so if you don't follow me there, that's normally where I make the decision about what I want to record this week,
sentences.zh: 我在Instagram上给了你们两个选项，所以如果你还没关注我，通常我会在那里决定这周要录什么内容，

sentences.en: and I gave you two options, either a bonus guest episode or an episode on microhabits, and here we are.
sentences.zh: 我给了两个选项，要么是嘉宾加更，要么是关于微习惯的一期，然后我们就选了这个。

sentences.en: You chose right.
sentences.zh: 你们选对了。

sentences.en: I'm very excited to be recording this today, and the research was so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我非常兴奋今天能录制这一期，研究过程太迷人了。

sentences.en: Some of the studies, some of the things that I found out, I was like, this is crazy.
sentences.zh: 有些研究，我发现的一些事情，当时我就觉得，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Like, I am learning so much.
sentences.zh: 就像，我学到了太多东西。

sentences.en: I also just want to say we hit a huge milestone this week, which was one million listeners, and I honestly still can't, like, fathom that.
sentences.zh: 我还想说，我们这周达成了一个巨大的里程碑，那就是达到了一百万听众，老实说，我到现在还是无法想象。

sentences.en: Like, I genuinely am so, like, honestly baffled, a bit confused, a bit overwhelmed, to be honest, that there are so many people listening to this show.
sentences.zh: 我真的感到非常，老实说，感到困惑，有点不知所措，说实话，竟然有这么多人收听这个节目。

sentences.en: Like, I started this as, like, a side project, as, like, a hobby, just to kind of verbalize the things that I was going through and to be able to have an outlet
sentences.zh: 我开始做这个节目时，就像是一个副业，一个爱好，只是为了把我的经历表达出来，并能有一个出口，

sentences.en: for the research I was doing and the things that I love to talk about with my wonderful friends.
sentences.zh: 来分享我所做的研究，以及我喜欢和好朋友们谈论的事情。

sentences.en: Shout out to them if they're listening.
sentences.zh: 如果她们在听的话，给她们打个招呼。

sentences.en: You guys are amazing.
sentences.zh: 你们太棒了。

sentences.en: And suddenly it has an audience, so it's been really unexpected, and I'm so grateful.
sentences.zh: 突然间它有了听众，所以这真的很出乎意料，我非常感激。

sentences.en: I think the other thing I've been really worried about is that as this show grows, it might become less authentic.
sentences.zh: 我想我担心的另一件事是，随着节目的成长，它可能会变得不那么真实。

sentences.en: I just, that's something that's really been on my mind.
sentences.zh: 我只是，这确实一直在我脑海里盘旋。

sentences.en: And what I want to be able to do is continue posting the things that I really want to talk about and that I hope other people want to hear about,
sentences.zh: 我想要做的是继续发布我真正想谈论的事情，并且我希望其他人也想听的事情，

sentences.en: not just things that I feel pressure I need to speak on or following trends.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅因为感到压力而必须谈论，或者盲目跟风。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I just don't want to lose that authenticity.
sentences.zh: 我只是不想失去那种真实感。

sentences.en: And I think that's why a lot of people listen to this because, I don't know, I'm someone in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么很多人听这个节目的原因，因为，我不知道，我只是一个20多岁的人。

sentences.en: I'm dealing with this stuff as we all are.
sentences.zh: 我正在处理这些事情，就像我们所有人一样。

sentences.en: So, I don't know, some of my fears and anxieties for the people who listen to the bonus episodes.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道，对于那些听加更节目的人来说，这算是我的一些恐惧和焦虑吧。

sentences.en: So, take away whatever you want from that.
sentences.zh: 所以，随你们怎么想吧。

sentences.en: But once again, thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 但再次感谢你们的收听。

sentences.en: Let's get into what we're talking about today, microhabits.
sentences.zh: 让我们进入今天的话题：微习惯。

sentences.en: It is such a fascinating, fascinating topic.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常、非常迷人的话题。

sentences.en: They've become, like the term microhabits has become quite a trendy saying or a trendy term or concept in wellness communities recently.
sentences.zh: 它们已经变得，就像“微习惯”这个词最近在健康社区里变成了一个非常时髦的说法、术语或概念。

sentences.en: And I think for mostly really, really good reasons.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这主要是出于非常、非常好的原因。

sentences.en: So, what they are is they are these small, simple actions that you're able to take every day or integrate into your life really easily that help you achieve big results.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们就是那些你每天都能做，或者很容易融入你生活的小而简单的行动，能帮助你取得巨大的成果。

sentences.en: They're basically just small habits, microhabits.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上就是小习惯，微习惯。

sentences.en: Sometimes when we think about, you know, big overhauls of our entire lifestyle, it can seem really overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 有时当我们想到，你知道，对整个生活方式进行大修时，可能会让人感到非常不知所措。

sentences.en: But we can use microhabits, which are just small actions that we can change day to day to transform, I think, any area, any facet of our lives
sentences.zh: 但我们可以利用微习惯，也就是我们每天可以改变的小行动，来转化，我认为，我们生活中的任何领域、任何方面，

sentences.en: that we might not be entirely satisfied with by starting really small, by starting from the ground up and keeping, you know, the end goal in sight.
sentences.zh: 如果我们对现状不完全满意，可以从很小的地方开始，从基础做起，并保持，你知道，最终目标在视野之内。

sentences.en: But making it easier for us to get there and to ease into those changes and those transformations and to ensure that the changes we want to make to our lives are sustainable.
sentences.zh: 但让实现目标变得更容易，让我们更容易适应这些改变和转化，并确保我们想要做出的生活改变是可持续的。

sentences.en: You know, there's no point putting a lot of effort into something, putting all your eggs in one basket, dedicating yourself entirely to some goal
sentences.zh: 你知道，在一件事情上投入大量精力，把所有鸡蛋放在一个篮子里，全身心投入到某个目标中，是毫无意义的，

sentences.en: if you're going to give up after one month because you're mentally and physically exhausted.
sentences.zh: 如果你因为身心俱疲而在一个月后就放弃了的话。

sentences.en: But microhabits are a really,
sentences.zh: 但微习惯是一个非常，

sentences.en: I think, sneaky, amazing way around that.
sentences.zh: 我认为，巧妙且神奇的解决方法。

sentences.en: And there's so much fascinating psychology around them.
sentences.zh: 而且围绕它们有太多迷人的心理学知识。

sentences.en: When we set ourselves big and ambitious and sometimes ambiguous goals, like, I don't know, I want to eat healthier or to be more active or fix my anxiety, make new friends.
sentences.zh: 当我们为自己设定宏大、雄心勃勃，有时又模糊不清的目标时，比如，我不知道，我想吃得更健康，或者更积极一点，或者解决我的焦虑，结交新朋友。

sentences.en: It can be super overwhelming to
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人感到非常不知所措，

sentences.en: A, try and stick to it.
sentences.zh: 第一，试图坚持下去。

sentences.en: B, figure out how we're going to achieve that goal through concrete steps.
sentences.zh: 第二，弄清楚我们如何通过具体的步骤来实现这个目标。

sentences.en: You know, saying something like, I want to make new friends.
sentences.zh: 你知道，说出“我想结交新朋友”这样的话。

sentences.en: It's such a scary and daunting goal.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常可怕和艰巨的目标。

sentences.en: Like, how do we actually get there?
sentences.zh: 我们到底该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: And I think it's really hard to know when your goal has been achieved.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为很难知道什么时候你的目标已经实现了。

sentences.en: How do you know when you're no longer anxious?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道你不再焦虑了？

sentences.en: How do you know when you're healthier?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道你更健康了？

sentences.en: Like, yes, you'll feel it.
sentences.zh: 是的，你会感觉到。

sentences.en: But how exactly did you get there?
sentences.zh: 但你到底是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: If the goal is this big, huge thing that you want and you're pining after and you get there and, you know, how do you know that you could do it again?
sentences.zh: 如果目标是你渴望的那个宏大的东西，当你达到它时，你知道，你怎么知道你还能再做一次？

sentences.en: How can you maintain those lifestyle changes?
sentences.zh: 你如何维持这些生活方式的改变？

sentences.en: I think big goals are always going to be really hard to achieve.
sentences.zh: 我认为宏大的目标总是很难实现。

sentences.en: Hence that saying, you know, if it was easy, everyone would do it.
sentences.zh: 所以才有那句老话，你知道，如果容易的话，每个人都会去做。

sentences.en: The reason is that they offer require major lifestyle overhaul and changes to our daily habits, which we've become rather attached to.
sentences.zh: 原因在于它们通常需要重大的生活方式调整和日常习惯的改变，而我们已经对这些习惯产生了依赖。

sentences.en: But what if you could achieve those exact same goals by just doing something small every day?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能通过每天只做一点小事来实现同样的目标呢？

sentences.en: That sounds, you know, kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 这听起来，你知道，相当神奇。

sentences.en: And that's the idea behind micro habits.
sentences.zh: 这就是微习惯背后的理念。

sentences.en: You are still able to make those big changes, but by making a series of small ones instead.
sentences.zh: 你仍然能够做出那些巨大的改变，但通过一系列小的改变来实现。

sentences.en: Tasks that are so small and so, you know, convenient that you don't even, you know, notice them half the time and you don't really have an excuse not to do them.
sentences.zh: 这些任务非常小，非常，你知道，方便，以至于你有一半时间甚至不会注意到它们，而且你真的没有借口不去完成它们。

sentences.en: And when you keep these small habits up and when you keep these promises to yourself, not only are you able to see progress and reach your goals sustainably, whilst also ensuring
sentences.zh: 当你坚持这些小习惯，当你遵守对自己的承诺时，你不仅能够看到进步并可持续地实现你的目标，同时还能确保

sentences.en: ensuring that your healthy habits stick, but you also gain confidence over time.
sentences.zh: 确保你的健康习惯能够坚持下去，而且随着时间的推移，你还会获得自信。

sentences.en: You know, I think when we set out to achieve big goals and we're really pushing so hard in those first few weeks and those first few months, when we are, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为当我们开始追求宏大目标，并且在最初的几周和几个月里非常努力地推进时，当我们，你知道，

sentences.en: we fail or we have a small setback, it can be really easy to see all that progress being, you know, to sense that that progress has been undone or to feel a sense of failure.
sentences.zh: 我们失败了或者遇到了一点挫折，很容易就会觉得所有的进步都被，你知道，感觉到那种进步被抵消了，或者产生一种失败感。

sentences.en: But micro habits allow us to achieve those goals over time and sustainably so that we're allowed to have small setbacks as long as we keep up these small habits.
sentences.zh: 但微习惯让我们能够随着时间的推移可持续地实现这些目标，这样即使我们遇到小挫折，只要我们保持这些小习惯，也没关系。

sentences.en: So let's talk about some examples.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们谈谈一些例子。

sentences.en: When I was doing this research and just from like my general
sentences.zh: 当我做这项研究时，仅仅从我个人的

sentences.en: overall view of how the term micro habits is used, they're often applied to, you know, fitness and weight loss and diet culture and physical health, which, of course, I appreciate
sentences.zh: 对“微习惯”一词使用方式的总体看法来看，它们通常被应用于，你知道，健身、减肥、节食文化和身体健康，当然，我很欣赏这一点，

sentences.en: and I think it's so important that people want to take care of themselves in whatever capacity that might be.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们想要以任何方式照顾好自己都非常重要。

sentences.en: But I kind of want to discuss them in other areas of our lives because I think that although a lot of the time
sentences.zh: 但我还是想在其他生活领域讨论它们，因为我认为尽管很多时候，

sentences.en: people, especially in our 20s, are really worried about how we look and whether we're active and whether we're physically healthy, sometimes it's not the only focus
sentences.zh: 人们，尤其是在我们20多岁的时候，非常担心我们的外表、是否活跃以及是否身体健康，但有时这并不是唯一的焦点，

sentences.en: and I kind of don't like to talk about that too much on my show.
sentences.zh: 而且我不太喜欢在我的节目中过多谈论这个。

sentences.en: I think it can contribute and easily become a discussion about things that actually are unhealthy and aren't for the best for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能会助长并轻易变成关于那些实际上不健康、对我们自身并非最好的事情的讨论。

sentences.en: So let's talk about some other areas.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们谈谈其他领域。

sentences.en: For example, if you want to start a podcast, what is a micro habit that can build that?
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你想开始做播客，什么微习惯可以建立起这个目标？

sentences.en: I get people asking me all the time, like I want to start a podcast and my first answer is always like, yes, absolutely, you should do it.
sentences.zh: 我经常被人问到，比如我想开始做播客，我的第一个回答总是，是的，绝对应该做。

sentences.en: There is room for everyone and you definitely have something to share.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有空间，你绝对有东西可以分享。

sentences.en: And the second question is and the second kind of statement is always like, how do I do it?
sentences.zh: 第二个问题，或者说第二种说法总是，我该怎么做？

sentences.en: A micro habit could be,
sentences.zh: 一个微习惯可以是，

sentences.en: I don't know, write 300, write down one idea every day for what you want to talk about on your show or record just one episode a week, even if you only do five minutes each day.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，写300字，每天写下一个你想在节目中谈论的想法，或者每周只录一期节目，即使你每天只做五分钟。

sentences.en: That's a really achievable goal.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常容易实现的目标。

sentences.en: You know, writing something down in your notes app once a day, some idea that you've had for content or for an episode, it's not going to take too much from you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每天在你的笔记应用里写点东西，一些你对内容或某一期的想法，这不会占用你太多时间。

sentences.en: It's not going to take too much effort and it's really doable.
sentences.zh: 这不会花费太多精力，而且非常可行。

sentences.en: Another one that I hear a lot from my friends is spending less time on social media.
sentences.zh: 我从朋友那里听到的另一个常见问题是减少在社交媒体上花费的时间。

sentences.en: What's a simple micro habit you can do for that?
sentences.zh: 有什么简单的微习惯可以做到这一点？

sentences.en: You know, put your, like make a promise to yourself, I can go on my phone as much as I want throughout the day, but I'm going to put it down at 10 p.m.
sentences.zh: 你知道，给自己一个承诺，我可以整天随心所欲地玩手机，但我会在晚上10点放下它。

sentences.en: Or between the hours of, you know, every 30 minutes, I have to turn my phone off, you know, for the rest of that half hour into the next, until the next hour.
sentences.zh: 或者在，你知道，每30分钟的时间段里，我必须关掉手机，你知道，在那半小时剩下的时间里，直到下一个小时。

sentences.en: Just so you have those small breaks or, okay, I want to slowly decrease the amount of pickups I have.
sentences.zh: 这样你就有那些小小的休息时间，或者，好吧，我想慢慢减少我拿起手机的次数。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: If you have an iPhone, you can see how many times you like pick up and you open a social media app, like Instagram or TikTok.
sentences.zh: 如果你有iPhone，你可以看到你一天拿起手机并打开社交媒体应用（如Instagram或TikTok）的次数。

sentences.en: Say that's like 50 times a day.
sentences.zh: 假设是每天50次。

sentences.en: Be like, okay, by tomorrow, I want it to be 49 and then maybe 48 and 47 next week.
sentences.zh: 那就说，好吧，到明天，我想把它变成49次，然后下周可能是48次、47次。

sentences.en: Not even like on a day-to-day, just trying to think about small things you can do, small goals you can set.
sentences.zh: 甚至不需要按天计算，只是试着思考你可以做的小事，可以设定的小目标。

sentences.en: But getting over heartbreak, that's a massive topic we talk about on the show because, you know, I think we all have been through that in our 20s
sentences.zh: 还有走出心碎，这是我们在节目中讨论的一个重大话题，因为，你知道，我认为我们20多岁的人都经历过这些，

sentences.en: and it's often really fucking brutal.
sentences.zh: 而且通常真的他妈的非常残酷。

sentences.en: How do we, you know, make sure that, how can we apply micro habits to heartbreak?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何，你知道，确保，我们如何将微习惯应用于心碎？

sentences.en: What about just checking their messages less, being like, okay, my only, the only thing I need to do today is to only check to see if they've messaged me once or twice.
sentences.zh: 比如少看他们的消息，告诉自己，好吧，我今天唯一需要做的就是只检查一两次他们是否给我发了消息。

sentences.en: Yes, I can't check it compulsively throughout the day, but I'm still allowed to because I still want to know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不能整天强迫性地检查，但我仍然被允许这样做，因为我还是想知道。

sentences.en: Or if you're getting over heartbreak, setting a goal of like, okay, well, I'm going to listen to one song I really, really love and just have like a wild dance,
sentences.zh: 或者如果你正在走出心碎，设定一个目标，比如，好吧，我要听一首我非常、非常喜欢的歌，然后疯狂地跳舞，

sentences.en: manic singing moment, just once a day to make myself feel better.
sentences.zh: 疯狂地唱歌，每天一次，让自己感觉好一点。

sentences.en: Another way that it's, I think micro habits are often applied is productivity and creativity.
sentences.zh: 我认为微习惯经常被应用的另一个领域是生产力和创造力。

sentences.en: As we enter into full-time work or we're struggling with uni and we have, you know, jobs and things to do and bills to pay and relationships to maintain
sentences.zh: 当我们进入全职工作，或者在学业中挣扎，我们有，你知道，工作要做，账单要付，人际关系要维护，

sentences.en: and, I don't know, cleaning, I don't know, whatever you're doing with your life, we're all pretty busy.
sentences.zh: 还有，我不知道，打扫卫生，我不知道，无论你在生活中做什么，我们都很忙。

sentences.en: And sometimes the first thing to go is the things that really fuel our soul, our creative passions and our hobbies.
sentences.zh: 有时，最先被我们抛弃的，往往是那些真正滋养我们灵魂的东西，比如我们的创造热情和爱好。

sentences.en: So maybe one of your micro habits, if you're someone who's realizing that they're a little bit disconnected from that creative right side of their brain is to, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你意识到自己与大脑右侧的创造力有些脱节，那么你的微习惯之一，可以是，你知道的，

sentences.en: read just one page of a book each night or simply list five things you're grateful for if you want to get into journaling or, you know, just only,
sentences.zh: 每晚读一页书，或者如果你想开始写日记，就简单地列出五件让你感恩的事，或者，你知道，仅仅是，

sentences.en: you only need to spend five minutes a day doing like a meditation or a yoga pose or watching a really interesting video that you can contribute to conversations with.
sentences.zh: 你每天只需要花五分钟做冥想、做一个瑜伽动作，或者看一个有趣的视频，让你在对话中能有谈资。

sentences.en: Those don't sound too hard, do they?
sentences.zh: 听起来并不难，对吧？

sentences.en: They sound really doable.
sentences.zh: 听起来真的很可行。

sentences.en: Everyone has five minutes in their day to do one small thing that might actually make your life a lot better.
sentences.zh: 每个人每天都有五分钟时间去做一件小事，而这件小事或许真的能让你的生活变得好很多。

sentences.en: And over time, these habits build and become bigger and we're able to challenge ourselves to set a new micro habit that actually feels a lot less significant
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这些习惯会积累并壮大，我们就能挑战自己去设定一个新的微习惯，而这个新习惯感觉起来要比

sentences.en: than if we'd started with that step to begin with.
sentences.zh: 我们一开始就迈出那一步要轻松得多。

sentences.en: Small blocks can still build really big towers and it's harder to take them apart, harder to take that final structure, that final lifestyle that you're looking for
sentences.zh: 小积木也能搭出高塔，而且要拆掉它们，要拆掉你最终追求的那个结构、那种生活方式，会变得更难，

sentences.en: apart if those habits that have contributed to it are really easy to do and are really sustainable.
sentences.zh: 如果构成它的那些习惯非常容易执行且具有可持续性的话。

sentences.en: So why are we talking about them today?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们今天为什么要谈论这些呢？

sentences.en: Why are we talking about them in the context of our 20s?
sentences.zh: 为什么要在我们二十多岁的背景下谈论它们呢？

sentences.en: I think personally, in our 20s, we have a responsibility to ourselves to decide what kind of lives we want to have.
sentences.zh: 我个人认为，在我们二十多岁时，我们有责任为自己决定想要过什么样的生活。

sentences.en: It's often I think when we begin to recognise unhealthy habits or patterns of thinking that might not be the healthiest, that may have come from our upbringing,
sentences.zh: 我认为，往往是在这个阶段，我们开始意识到那些可能不太健康的习惯或思维模式，它们可能源于我们的教养，

sentences.en: may have come from our childhood.
sentences.zh: 可能源于我们的童年。

sentences.en: If you want to listen to the childhood trauma episode, we talk about this a little bit more about how our perspectives and our ways that we see ourselves
sentences.zh: 如果你想听关于童年创伤的那期节目，我们在那里更深入地探讨了我们的视角、我们看待自己的方式，

sentences.en: and the habits that we form really do begin in our early infancy even.
sentences.zh: 以及我们形成的习惯，其实早在婴儿时期就开始了。

sentences.en: But when we get to adulthood, when we get to our 20s, we might want to improve ourselves for the better.
sentences.zh: 但当我们步入成年，当我们到了二十多岁，我们可能会想要让自己变得更好。

sentences.en: We have the emotional and the mental capacity to recognise what's not working, to have self-awareness.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有情感和心理能力去识别哪些行不通，去拥有自我意识。

sentences.en: I feel like many of the people who listen to this show are doing so out of an eagerness to improve themselves, their wellbeing and their lives or because there's something
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多听这个节目的听众，都是出于渴望改善自我、提升幸福感和生活质量，或者是因为他们

sentences.en: they're struggling with in their day-to-day lives.
sentences.zh: 在日常生活中正面临某些挣扎。

sentences.en: Honestly,
sentences.zh: 老实说，

sentences.en: no matter your circumstances,
sentences.zh: 无论你的处境如何，

sentences.en: whatever you're going through right now, implementing these daily micro habits can actually lead to massive improvements no matter what area of your life you want to change
sentences.zh: 无论你现在正在经历什么，实施这些日常微习惯确实能带来巨大的改善，无论你想改变

sentences.en: or improve.
sentences.zh: 或提升生活的哪个领域。

sentences.en: One of the micro habits that I've set myself recently is I found that because I work full-time and I'm doing this podcast and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我最近为自己设定的微习惯之一是，因为我全职工作，还要做这个播客，你知道，

sentences.en: I've got to keep up with, you know, my chores and with my friends and trying to be active,
sentences.zh: 我得处理家务，还要和朋友保持联系，还要努力保持运动，

sentences.en: the one thing that's kind of fallen off the radar is being physically active and feeling like my body is doing what I want it to do.
sentences.zh: 唯一被我忽略的事情就是身体锻炼，以及那种感觉身体状态如我所愿的感觉。

sentences.en: So I've set this micro habit of like anytime I want to go into the office and my office is in the city, I have to walk in.
sentences.zh: 所以我设定了一个微习惯：只要我想去办公室，而我的办公室在市中心，我就必须步行去。

sentences.en: It's a 45-minute walk.
sentences.zh: 那是一段45分钟的步行路程。

sentences.en: It's not that far.
sentences.zh: 其实并不远。

sentences.en: It takes like 35 minutes on the train and that's a really easy habit to implement for me because it's not every day that I have to do it and it's really small.
sentences.zh: 坐火车要35分钟，对我来说这是一个非常容易实施的习惯，因为我不需要每天都这么做，而且它真的很小。

sentences.en: It's really doable and it's really rewarding as well.
sentences.zh: 它真的很可行，而且也很有回报感。

sentences.en: I think we do often think of physical health when we think of lifestyle change but it can be so much more than that.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在考虑生活方式改变时，往往会想到身体健康，但它远不止于此。

sentences.en: We can use micro habits to reduce anxiety, promote our sleep, be more productive, creative, get over a bad breakup, make more connections.
sentences.zh: 我们可以利用微习惯来减轻焦虑、促进睡眠、提高效率、激发创造力、走出失恋阴影、建立更多联系。

sentences.en: Their beauty is in their simplicity but also their universality.
sentences.zh: 它们的魅力在于其简单性，也在于其普适性。

sentences.en: They're so easy to integrate into our lives and into really any area of our lives.
sentences.zh: 它们非常容易融入我们的生活，融入我们生活的任何领域。

sentences.en: So let's talk about why they work and really hyping these up today and making them sound like some kind of universal antidote but there's a reason why micro habits are a lot easier
sentences.zh: 所以让我们谈谈它们为什么有效。今天我确实在极力推崇它们，让它们听起来像某种万能解药，但微习惯之所以更容易

sentences.en: to implement and I know it sounds intuitive but there's some stronger science backing it as well.
sentences.zh: 实施是有原因的，我知道这听起来很直观，但背后也有更强的科学依据。

sentences.en: Basically,
sentences.zh: 基本上，

sentences.en: they limit how often we can apply an all or nothing mindset and consequently the likelihood of failure.
sentences.zh: 它们限制了我们采用“非黑即白”思维的频率，从而降低了失败的可能性。

sentences.en: So the all or nothing mindset, it's a way of thinking that kind of relies on extremes and particularly the extreme of either success or failure.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“非黑即白”思维，是一种依赖极端的思维方式，特别是成功或失败这两个极端。

sentences.en: You know, you've got this goal in mind and you're either doing everything completely right, you meet your goal instantly, you're sticking with all of your habits,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你心里有这个目标，要么你一切都做得完全正确，立刻达成目标，坚持所有习惯，

sentences.en: you're doing everything you need to do perfectly all the time or you don't do that, you make a slip up, you forget to do something and you fail, you can't go forward, that's done.
sentences.zh: 要么你必须完美地完成所有需要做的事，否则一旦你没做到，犯了错，忘记做某事，你就失败了，你就无法继续，一切就完了。

sentences.en: You know, like it's success or failure and there's nothing
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像是成功或失败，没有中间地带。

sentences.en: all or nothing thinking usually leads to really unrealistic standards for yourself and for others and it's really hard to maintain motivation because we're humans,
sentences.zh: 非黑即白的思维通常会导致对自己和他人产生非常不切实际的标准，而且很难保持动力，因为我们是人类，

sentences.en: we're going to make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 我们难免会犯错。

sentences.en: Life gets in the way of implementing healthy habits and this type of thinking, it's known as a cognitive distortion, which essentially is an exaggerated pattern of thought
sentences.zh: 生活总会阻碍我们养成健康的习惯，而这种思维方式被称为认知扭曲，本质上是一种夸大的思维模式，

sentences.en: and of thinking
sentences.zh: 一种思维方式，

sentences.en: that derails our progress and can lead us to viewing things in a way that's false to how they truly are.
sentences.zh: 它会破坏我们的进步，导致我们以一种偏离事实的方式看待事物。

sentences.en: You know, say that one of your goals is like, oh, I want to use social media less and you're being really strict, you're like only an hour a day and that's that and then one day
sentences.zh: 比如，假设你的目标之一是“我想少用社交媒体”，你对自己要求很严，规定每天只能用一小时，就这么定了。然后有一天，

sentences.en: you go over an hour to hour and five minutes and you're like, well, I've ruined it,
sentences.zh: 你用了一个小时零五分钟，你就会觉得：好吧，我搞砸了，

sentences.en: I've ruined it, like this shows that I don't have self-discipline and I can't meet my goal and this all-or-nothing distortion is exactly what we're talking about in this instance.
sentences.zh: 我彻底毁了，这说明我没有自律，我无法达成目标。这种非黑即白的扭曲正是我们在这个例子中所谈论的。

sentences.en: If we engage too frequently in this style of thinking, particularly when we're trying to achieve a goal, it can be really difficult to forgive our failures, to make progress
sentences.zh: 如果我们过于频繁地陷入这种思维方式，特别是在试图实现目标时，就很难原谅自己的失败，很难取得进步，

sentences.en: or feel satisfied and ensure that the goal is sustainable because we're always going to make mistakes, we are, you know, forgetful creatures, we are funny creatures,
sentences.zh: 或者感到满足，并确保目标具有可持续性。因为我们总会犯错，我们是健忘的生物，我们是滑稽的生物，

sentences.en: we're messy creatures but micro habits, they're able to interrupt that extreme way of thinking, that feedback loop of success or failure.
sentences.zh: 我们是混乱的生物。但微习惯能够打断那种极端的思维方式，打断那种成功或失败的反馈循环。

sentences.en: We're able to not only have smaller successes but teach ourselves that our energy does not need to be a hundred and million percent committed and tied to one goal
sentences.zh: 我们不仅能够获得小小的成功，还能教会自己：我们的精力不需要百分之百、甚至百分之万地投入并绑定在一个目标上，

sentences.en: with no slip-ups allowed.
sentences.zh: 且不允许任何差错。

sentences.en: They allow us to break things down into smaller, bite-sized pieces which we know are easier for our brains to digest and they're easier to implement because they require
sentences.zh: 它们让我们把事情分解成更小、更易消化的碎片，我们知道这更容易被大脑接受，也更容易实施，因为它们需要

sentences.en: less challenge and less change and we're more likely to be successful.
sentences.zh: 更少的挑战和改变，我们也更有可能成功。

sentences.en: So the other reason they work is to do with dopamine.
sentences.zh: 所以它们有效的另一个原因与多巴胺有关。

sentences.en: I know we talk about dopamine so often on this show like all the time but it's because it's so crucial to so many of our behaviors and our actions and our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 我知道在这个节目里我们经常谈论多巴胺，总是谈论，但这是因为它对我们的许多行为、行动和日常生活至关重要。

sentences.en: it's like it is the one of the most important neurotransmitters we have in our artillery.
sentences.zh: 它就像是我们武器库中最重要的神经递质之一。

sentences.en: Often the habits we see as being unhealthy
sentences.zh: 通常我们认为不健康的习惯，

sentences.en: I'm going to use the TikTok example again like scrolling TikTok for hours
sentences.zh: 我又要用TikTok举例了，比如睡前刷几个小时TikTok，

sentences.en: TikTok don't sue me because I'm defaming you or whatever but you know scrolling TikTok for hours before bed or sleeping in or eating food that makes us feel bad.
sentences.zh: TikTok别起诉我诽谤啊，但你知道，睡前刷几个小时TikTok，或者睡懒觉，或者吃让我们感觉糟糕的食物。

sentences.en: These habits actually bring us some form of dopamine like we get a dopamine hit or we feel comfortable so when we attempt to interrupt those habits and overhaul our lives
sentences.zh: 这些习惯实际上确实给我们带来某种形式的多巴胺，比如我们得到了多巴胺刺激，或者感到舒适。所以当我们试图打断这些习惯并彻底改变生活时，

sentences.en: not only do we prevent activities that our brain actually relies on for dopamine the chemical that motivates us and creates pleasant feelings and stability but we also alter our
sentences.zh: 我们不仅阻止了大脑实际上依赖多巴胺（这种激励我们并产生愉悦感和稳定性的化学物质）的活动，而且我们还改变了我们的

sentences.en: mental comfort space and that's kind of the area that's like the things that make our brain feel safe and often routine habits even if they cause long-term damage do make us
sentences.zh: 心理舒适区。那是一个让大脑感到安全的区域，通常常规习惯即使造成长期损害，也确实让我们

sentences.en: feel safe
sentences.zh: 感到安全。

sentences.en: and often that causes us to withdraw back into our old habits quicker when we are challenged with other possibly you know uncomfortable situations in the external world I think
sentences.zh: 而这往往导致我们在外部世界面临其他可能令人不适的情况时，更快地退回到旧习惯中。我想

sentences.en: we see this so often people set out with big goals for example to quit drinking or stop smoking like cold turkey but those habits bring comfort and dopamine and serotonin
sentences.zh: 我们经常看到这种情况，人们设定了宏大的目标，例如彻底戒酒或戒烟，但这些习惯带来了舒适、多巴胺和血清素，

sentences.en: so as soon as something else challenges us and we no longer have that you know that stability that's created by that habit we're likely to fall straight back into them you know
sentences.zh: 所以一旦有其他事情挑战我们，而我们不再拥有那种由习惯带来的稳定性时，我们很可能会直接退回到旧习惯中，你知道的。

sentences.en: but if we say instead of like I'm going to completely quit drinking and then you know you go through a breakup or you know you get a parking fine or you have a
sentences.zh: 但如果我们说，与其说“我要彻底戒酒”，然后你知道，你经历了一次失恋，或者你收到了一张停车罚单，或者你遇到了一件

sentences.en: shit on it what if we instead said you know
sentences.zh: 倒霉事，如果我们换个说法，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm going to drink one less drink than I normally would on a night out or I'm only going to drink drinks with lower levels of alcohol or only drink one to two days a week we give
